message.content: The kernel computes expm1 via range reduction (floor(x·log2e+0.5) exponent, split-ln2 reduction, degree-6 polynomial, 2^e scale). The domain is tiny — all finite FP16 values in [-10,10] — so I can exhaustively test every legal input against the FP64 reference.

Every output element must satisfy abs(actual[i] - target[i]) <= 1e-7 + 1e-6 * abs(target[i])."}], "statement": "The kernel's output violates the contract tolerance abs(actual-target) <= 1e-7 + 1e-6*|target| for at least one finite FP16 input in [-10,10]."}

message.reasoning_content:
The kernel: expm1 via range reduction with 2^exponent scale. Concern: exponent = floor(x*log2e + 0.5) — near x=0, exponent=0, scale=1, value = (1-1)+1*local = local — fine. But precision: ln2 split constants: 0.69313812256 + 0.0000090580006145 = 0.6931471805606145 ≈ ln2 (0.6931471805599453). Good.

Issue: for negative exponent large (x=-10, exponent=floor(-13.28+0.5)=floor(-12.78)=-13), exponent+127=114, fine. For x=10, exponent=floor(14.93)=14, +127=141 fine.

Tolerance is tight: 1e-7 + 1e-6*|target|. Polynomial degree 6? Actually it's reduced + reduced²*(...): terms up to reduced^7? local = reduced + reduced²*(0.5 + c3*r + ...). Wait: reduced + r²*poly where poly ends with ...*r+0.5 → local = r + 0.5r² + c3 r³ ... up to r⁷/5040 approx (coefficients like Taylor). But local_value should be exp(r)-1 ≈ r + r²/2 + ... For expm1 computed as (scale-1) + scale*local: catastrophic cancellation when scale≈1 (r small): (1-1)+1*local, fine since scale-1 exactly 0 and local computed directly. When exponent ≠0, scale-1 exact, scale*local — the error is roughly relative error of scale*exp(r) ~ few ulps plus polynomial error. Polynomial error: using only up to r⁷? coefficients: 0.16667 (should be 1/6=0.1666667, using 0.16667 slightly off), 0.041666666666666664=1/24, 1/120=0.008333..., 1/720=0.0013888... So local ≈ r + r²/2 + r³/6(0.16667 approx) ... degree: poly has 4 coefficients after 0.5: gives terms r³...r⁷? local = r + r²*p, p = 1/5040 r⁴... wait p = ((((1/720 r + 1/120)r + 1/24)r + 1/6)r + 1/2). So local = r + r²/2 + r³/6 + r⁴/24 + r⁵/120 + r⁶/720. Missing r⁷/5040. |r| ≤ ln2/2 ≈ 0.3466. r⁷/5040 ≈ 0.3466^7/5040 ≈ 6e-7/5040 ≈ 1.2e-10. Fine. Coefficient 0.16667 vs 1/6 error 3.3e-6 relative on r³/6 term: r³/6 ≈ 0.00695, error 3.3e-6*0.00695≈2.3e-8. Also 1/5040 missing. And reduced range: |r| ≤ ~0.347 plus reduction error from ln2 approximation. Also cancellation in (scale-1)+scale*local when exponent=±1? For exponent=0, scale=1 exact, value=local — but local polynomial error relative to expm1(r) with r=|x|≤0.5(log2e+0.5 boundary: exponent 0 when |x log2e +0.5|<1 → x in about [-0.721, 0.721)). local error ~1e-8 vs tolerance 1e-7. Plausibly fine. But best to test exhaustively: all finite FP16 values in [-10,10] is only ~15k values — can test entire domain! Great plan.

Also check negative subnormals/zero: x=0 → exponent=0, local=0, value 0 ✓. Tiny subnormal: fine.

Concern: FP32 rounding of x from FP16 exact. Also enable_fp_fusion=False. Also the reduction r error: ln2 constant sum = 0.69314718056... true ln2 = 0.6931471805599453; sum = 0.6931471805606145, off by 6.7e-13, times 14 → negligible.

But one real risk: for x near -0.721 boundary or generally the accuracy of (scale-1)+scale*local in FP32: relative error target 1e-6 relative for large |target| (target up to e^10-1≈22025, tolerance ≈2.2e-2 — very loose). Tight case: target near zero, i.e., x near 0 (|x|<0.7): error must be ≤1e-7 + 1e-6|expm1(x)|. There local is computed directly, error ~1e-8-ish. Should pass but run exhaustive test.

Record claim, run probe on all 15k+ FP16 values in [-10,10].
